- `/output/punycode.mjs` exports `punycodeEncode(label)` (unicode string of ONE label, no dots -> ASCII string) and `punycodeDecode(ascii)` (punycode ASCII string -> unicode string). RFC 3492 with base=36, tmin=1, tmax=26, skew=38, damp=700, initial_bias=72, initial_n=128, delimiter '-'.

- Invalid domains (e.g. containing `_`, empty labels, empty domain) raise IDNAError-ish errors and the process exits with code 1 after printing an error to stderr.

Details: punycodeEncode takes a unicode label string, emits the basic code points (ASCII) verbatim, then '-' delimiter if any basic chars were emitted, then encodes non-basic code points with the standard adaptive bias algorithm (parameters in the contract). punycodeDecode reverses it. Verify pyBytesRepr("xn--caf-dma.fr") === "b'xn--caf-dma.fr'".

Create `/output/idna.mjs` implementing the IDNA layer exactly per the interface contract, importing `{ punycodeEncode, punycodeDecode }` from './punycode.mjs' (another agent writes that file to this exact contract — do not create or modify it; for your own testing you may create a scratch copy under /tmp). `alabel(label)` (label is a JS unicode string): 1) If label is pure ASCII (all code points < 0x80): call `ulabel(label)` for validation (ignore its return), throw IDNAError('Label too long') if label.length > 63, else return the label unchanged. 2) Otherwise: if label is empty throw IDNAError('No Input'); run checkLabel(label) (throws on invalid); ascii = 'xn--' + punycodeEncode(label); throw IDNAError('Label too long') if ascii.length > 63; return ascii.

`ulabel(labelAscii)` (JS string, may be ASCII or unicode): 1) If it is NOT pure ASCII: checkLabel(label); return label unchanged. 2) Otherwise lowercase the WHOLE string. 3) If it starts with 'xn--': strip the prefix, punycodeDecode the rest, checkLabel the result, return it. 4) Else: checkLabel(label); return the lowercased ASCII string.

`idnaEncode(domain)`: if domain is empty -> throw IDNAError('Empty domain'). Split on '.' AND the unicode dots U+3002 U+FF0E U+FF61. Remove leading empty labels. If the last label is empty, drop it and remember trailing_dot. If nothing remains -> IDNAError('Empty domain'). For each remaining label, alabel(it) (an empty middle label therefore errors via alabel->ulabel->checkLabel with 'Empty Label'). Join with '.' (re-append empty label if trailing_dot). If total length >= 253 -> IDNAError('Domain too long'). Return ASCII string.

`idnaDecode(domain)`: same splitting (incl. unicode dots), strip leading empties and trailing empty (remember trailing_dot), empty -> IDNAError('Empty domain'), ulabel each label, join with '.', re-append '' if trailing_dot.

checkLabel(label): throw IDNAError('Empty Label') if empty. Throw IDNAError('Label must not start or end with a hyphen')-style error if it starts or ends with '-' (Python message: 'Label must not start or end with a hyphen'). For each char: if it is ASCII, it must be in [A-Za-z0-9-] — anything else (including '_', '.', space, control chars) throws InvalidCodepoint-like IDNAError with EXACT message format: `Codepoint U+XXXX at position N of '<label>' not allowed` where U+XXXX is the uppercase 4+-digit hex codepoint and N is the 1-based position (e.g. `Codepoint U+005F at position 4 of 'foo_bar' not allowed`). Test yourself with a scratch punycode implementation in /tmp or inline test vectors: alabel('café') -> 'xn--caf-dma'; ulabel('xn--caf-dma') -> 'café'; alabel('EXAMPLE') -> 'EXAMPLE'; ulabel('EXAMPLE') -> 'example'; idnaEncode('программирование.рф') -> 'xn--80aafcnpc2aandfgoce.xn--p1ai'; idnaDecode of that -> 'программирование.рф'; idnaEncode('example。com') -> 'example.com'; alabel('foo_bar') throws 'Codepoint U+005F at position 4 of \'foo_bar\' not allowed'.
